B0420.d: No public J2012 list carries B0420 with this meaning, and no carmaker describes an audio-system fault under it. The one documented use is unrelated: Saab files B0420 06 in the 9-3 (2003–2012) climate control as an open or grounded circuit to the right air-mix flap motor, which upsets temperature control.
s: No sound from any speaker, or the radio restarts by itself
Head unit freezes or ignores its buttons
Code stored together with other infotainment faults
c: high
Internal electronics or software of the head unit faulty
medium
Low or unstable supply voltage or poor ground at the head unit
low
Unit overheated because of blocked ventilation behind the dash

B0425.d: Every accessible J2012 list lacks B0425, and no maker's literature mentions it, leaving the code itself unverified. The title concerns a fault inside the separate audio amplifier rather than in its wiring.
s: No sound or only very low volume from the amplified speakers
Crackling, hum or distortion, often worse when warm
Subwoofer or premium sound channels drop out
c: high
Output stage or internal electronics of the amplifier failed
medium
Amplifier overheated, e.g. under a seat or in the boot without airflow
medium
Moisture or water in the amplifier housing or plug
low
Shorted speaker or wiring that has overloaded the output stage

B0440.d: No public J2012 source lists B0440, and no carmaker explains it, so the code cannot be verified. The title concerns the Bluetooth unit that pairs a phone for hands-free calls and music streaming.
s: Phone cannot be paired or is not found
Hands-free calls drop or music streaming stops
Bluetooth menu greyed out or missing
c: high
Software fault or hung state of the Bluetooth/telematics unit
medium
Bluetooth chip or its module failed internally
low
Poor supply or ground connection at the module

B0445.d: B0445 does not appear in any reachable J2012 list and is not described by a manufacturer, so its existence is unproven. A USB hub in the car splits one host port of the head unit across several sockets for media and charging.
s: USB stick or phone not recognised
Socket charges but transfers no data, or vice versa
Phone projection drops out repeatedly
c: high
Socket damaged or contaminated, short between pins
medium
Cable between hub and head unit loose or chafed
medium
Hub electronics or protection switch failed
low
Connected device or cable draws too much current

B0450.d: The code B0450 is absent from the publicly accessible J2012 lists, and no carmaker publishes it, so it remains unverified. Its title covers the hands-free microphone line.
s: Caller cannot hear the driver during hands-free calls
Voice control does not react to spoken commands
Emergency call or telematics status lamp shows a fault
c: high
Microphone in the headliner or mirror failed
medium
Microphone wire pinched or broken in the headliner or A-pillar
medium
Plug at microphone or module loose or corroded

B0455.d: No J2012 list available to the public includes B0455, and factory literature is silent on it, so the code is unverified. It names an internal fault of a display module, such as the centre screen or a cluster panel, not its wiring or data link.
s: Screen stays black, flickers or freezes on one picture
Touch input or buttons on the display do not respond
Information moves to another display or a warning appears
c: high
Display controller or panel electronics failed
medium
Software fault, often curable by an update
low
Button on the display unit jammed and reported as a fault

B0460.d: B0460 appears in none of the accessible J2012 lists and in no manufacturer document, so it remains unproven. Its title concerns the Bluetooth antenna circuit.
s: Phone pairs only at very short distance or not at all
Bluetooth switched off by the module, status lamp red
Calls and streaming break up repeatedly
c: high
Antenna contact or plug at the module loose or corroded
medium
Antenna or its lead damaged, e.g. after work behind the dash
low
Antenna detection or radio stage inside the module faulty

B0490.d: B0490 is not listed in any accessible J2012 source, nor does a carmaker's literature cover it, so public proof is lacking. The title covers the backlight of a display, today usually LED strings fed by a boost driver.
s: Screen dark although content is faintly visible in bright light
Brightness cannot be adjusted or follows no day/night change
Uneven, flickering or partly dark backlight
c: high
LED string or single LED of the backlight failed
medium
Backlight driver or its boost stage defective
low
Brightness control line open or shorted
